headline: Keane's goal-line role has quietly taken over
story: Keane's goal-line opportunity share has risen from 24% to 58% over three games, overtaking the incumbent back.

context.prior_baseline: Incumbent RB controlled 68% prior to Week 4

alternate_explanations.explanation: Incumbent RB was limited by a minor ankle issue in Week 4
alternate_explanations.test: Did the shift persist after the incumbent returned to full practice participation?
alternate_explanations.result: Incumbent returned to full practice Week 5; Keane still received 5 of 7 goal-line opportunities in Weeks 5-6

confirmation.supporting_signals: Snap share and red-zone target share both rose for Keane over the same window

judgment.what_we_know: The goal-line role shift persisted after the incumbent's injury-related absence resolved
judgment.what_we_dont_know: Whether this reflects a permanent depth-chart decision or an extended trial
judgment.evidence_significance: The shift persisted after the most obvious alternate cause resolved, strengthening the case that this represents a genuine, durable role change

significance.rationale: Major role reallocation on a core scoring situation, sustained across 3 games

evidence_strength.rationale: Full completeness, WEAKENED alternate explanation, 11-opportunity sample

betting_relevance.rationale: Directly reprices ATTD interpretation; market has already moved meaningfully

novelty.rationale: First season this back has held a lead role; genuinely new information relative to prior_history

story_tension.rationale: Grounded in a tested, WEAKENED alternate explanation plus supporting signal convergence

audience_relevance.rationale: Moderate name recognition; positional prominence heuristic, no defaulted fields

expected_stress_target: Confirms a genuinely strong, well-grounded story is recognized and eligible for the Big One — the baseline case every other fixture is contrasted against. Note: this fixture's gates are big_one_eligible: true AND watchlist_eligible: true simultaneously — it is also the double-gate stress case. Correct behavior is exactly one stories[] entry (Big One), with no second entry in Watchlist even though it independently clears that gate too. A cross_references[] pointer from Watchlist back to it is acceptable; a second full entry is not.

headline: Denver's red-zone tendencies may be shifting
story: A single-week sample shows a higher pass rate inside the 10 than the season average.

change.what_changed: Red-zone pass rate above season average in one game

alternate_explanations.explanation: Team trailed by 17 points for most of the second half, which independently increases pass rate regardless of any real tendency shift
alternate_explanations.evidence: Game script shows a 17-point deficit from late in the 2nd quarter onward
alternate_explanations.test: Does the pass-rate shift hold once game-script (score differential) is accounted for?
alternate_explanations.result: Sample is too small (6 plays, one game state) to separate a real tendency shift from a game-script effect

confirmation.supporting_signals: None available beyond this single game
confirmation.contradicting_signals: 5-game baseline shows no trend in this direction prior to this game
confirmation.market_reaction: Not applicable — no market tied to this signal type

judgment.what_we_know: One game showed an elevated red-zone pass rate under trailing-script conditions
judgment.what_we_dont_know: Whether this reflects any real coaching tendency shift at all, given the sample can't be separated from game script
judgment.evidence_significance: Single-game sample confounded by game script means this cannot yet be distinguished from a normal trailing-team pass-rate spike

significance.rationale: One game, small sample, plausible confound — banded as small, not material

evidence_strength.rationale: NOT_TESTABLE status, single-game sample, real confound identified

betting_relevance.rationale: Would matter if real, but confound means interpretation shouldn't change yet

novelty.rationale: A real deviation from the 5-game baseline, even if its cause is unclear

story_tension.rationale: Surface-level tension (baseline vs. this game) exists but is capped by the ungrounded/NOT_TESTABLE challenge

audience_relevance.rationale: Team-level story, moderate general interest, no defaulted fields

expected_stress_target: Evidence Strength (21) fails the Big One floor (40), so the gate correctly excludes it — but Novelty (58) and Story Tension (62) are both high enough that a naive 'exciting-sounding story' read could tempt the Editor toward the Big One anyway if it weren't respecting gates as authoritative. Watchlist also correctly fails since Evidence Strength (21) is below the Watchlist's own floor (25). Correct outcome: excluded entirely, or at most one flagged line in a lower section — never narrated as a discovered tendency shift.

headline: Carolina's slot coverage may be a soft spot — or may just be facing good slot receivers
story: Opposing slot receivers have out-produced expectation against Carolina in 2 of the last 3 games.

change.what_changed: Slot-receiver production above expectation against this defense

context.prior_baseline: Roughly at expectation over the first 4 weeks of the season

alternate_explanations.explanation: The two elevated games came against two of the league's better slot receivers, so this may reflect opponent quality rather than a defensive weakness
alternate_explanations.evidence: Both opposing slot receivers rank top-8 in the league in slot production this season
alternate_explanations.test: Was the third game (the one at expectation) against a weaker slot receiver, consistent with opponent quality driving the pattern rather than a real defensive issue?
alternate_explanations.result: Yes — the at-expectation game came against a bottom-half slot receiver, which is consistent with either explanation and doesn't clearly separate them

confirmation.supporting_signals: None distinguishing — coverage scheme data isn't available to separate personnel quality from scheme vulnerability
confirmation.contradicting_signals: The at-expectation game is itself a data point against a real, persistent vulnerability
confirmation.market_reaction: Not applicable — no market tied to this signal type

judgment.what_we_know: Slot production against this defense has been elevated in 2 of 3 recent games
judgment.what_we_dont_know: Whether this reflects a real defensive vulnerability or simply facing stronger slot receivers in those two games — the available data cannot distinguish these
judgment.evidence_significance: The alternate explanation was tested and the result doesn't clearly favor either the vulnerability read or the opponent-quality read — this remains genuinely unresolved, not weak evidence for a vulnerability

significance.rationale: A real, meaningful deviation from baseline, banded as meaningful given the magnitude and 3-game window

evidence_strength.rationale: UNRESOLVED status — tested but inconclusive, small downward adjustment from base completeness

betting_relevance.rationale: Would matter for opposing slot-receiver props if confirmed, but genuine ambiguity limits how strongly to lean on it

novelty.rationale: A real deviation from the season's first-month baseline

story_tension.rationale: Real tension between two plausible explanations that the data can't yet separate — grounded, not manufactured

audience_relevance.rationale: Team-defense-level story, lower general interest, no defaulted fields

expected_stress_target: Both gates pass, which is correct — this is a legitimately uncertain but real story, not a weak one. The test is whether the Editor's prose honestly represents the UNRESOLVED status (two plausible explanations, genuinely can't distinguish yet) rather than picking a side and writing it as either 'Carolina has a real weakness' or 'this is nothing, just matchups.' Correct placement is primarily the Watchlist — 'something worth tracking, not yet confirmed either way.' UPDATED (duplicate-detection two-case rule): a brief cross-reference to this story from another section (e.g. naming it in passing while covering something else) is now explicitly correct, not a violation — but only ONE section may give it a full treatment with its own eps_scores/provenance block. A second full retelling of the same argument in a different section (e.g. an independent What Changed entry making the same case a second time) is the actual failure this fixture now tests for.

headline: Osei's red-zone role held even after the starter's return
story: Osei's red-zone snap share rose while the starting TE was out, and has only partially receded now that the starter is back.

change.what_changed: Red-zone snap share increase, partial retention after starter's return

context.prior_baseline: 12% prior to starter's injury in Week 6

alternate_explanations.explanation: Starting TE's injury explains the entire increase, and the role should fully revert now that he's back
alternate_explanations.evidence: Starting TE missed Weeks 6-8 with a hamstring injury, returned Week 9
alternate_explanations.test: Did Osei's red-zone share fully revert to the 12% baseline in Week 9, or did some of the gain persist?
alternate_explanations.result: Osei's share dropped from 34% to 26% after the starter's return — a partial reversion, not a full one

confirmation.supporting_signals: Offensive coordinator has used more two-TE red-zone personnel since Week 9 than the season's first 5 weeks
confirmation.contradicting_signals: The share did drop meaningfully (34% to 26%), so the injury explanation isn't fully rejected — this is a partial result
confirmation.market_reaction: ATTD price moved from +1100 to +850, a modest but real shift

judgment.what_we_know: The role gain partially outlasted the injury that originally caused it, and personnel usage data supports a real if modest permanent change
judgment.what_we_dont_know: Whether the 26% level is the new stable rate or still settling
judgment.evidence_significance: The alternate explanation (injury fully explains it) was weakened but not eliminated — some of the shift appears durable, some appears to have been temporary

significance.rationale: A real, moderate role change — meaningful but not major given the partial reversion

evidence_strength.rationale: WEAKENED status but with an honest contradicting signal noted, so the adjustment is moderate, not maximal

betting_relevance.rationale: Real but modest reinterpretation of price, matching the modest market movement already observed

novelty.rationale: Genuinely new information, though the magnitude is moderate rather than surprising

story_tension.rationale: Grounded in a real, partial WEAKENED result — an honest 'partly durable, partly temporary' tension, not a clean survival story

audience_relevance.rationale: TE, lower general audience prominence, no defaulted fields

expected_stress_target: Deliberately contrasts with Fixture 1's clean WEAKENED result — this one is WEAKENED but with a real contradicting signal (partial, not full, reversion), and the evidence_significance field explicitly says so. Tests whether the Editor's prose can express a partial, honest result ('some of this held, some of it didn't') rather than flattening every WEAKENED status into the same confident 'survived the test' framing Fixture 1 earns. If the Editor writes this identically to Fixture 1, that's a failure to reason from the specific interrogation content rather than just the status label.
